name: Oregonator BZ Reaction
description: Three-variable dimensionless Oregonator teaching adaptation implementing Field (2007), equations 4–6. HBrO2, Bromide and Ce4_plus represent scaled concentrations, not molar concentrations. The prior file contained no derivatives. All existing initial concentrations and epsilon=.01,q=.001,f=1 inputs are retained; the previously missing epsilon_prime=1.98e-5 is explicitly supplied from Field's illustrative kinetic scaling. These mixed teaching inputs are not a calibrated reproduction of a chemical experiment. Radau integrates the stiff bromide timescale. The default observation window is 30 scaled time units (formerly 300 in the inert shell) at output interval 0.01 to demonstrate several cycles within the service work budget; independent 300-unit stiff integration remains finite and positive, but a full 300-unit server run exceeds the current work budget.

flows.name: HBrO2_Change
flows.equation: (q * Bromide - HBrO2 * Bromide + HBrO2 * (1 - HBrO2)) / epsilon

flows.name: Bromide_Change
flows.equation: (-q * Bromide - HBrO2 * Bromide + f * Ce4_plus) / epsilon_prime

reference: Field RJ (2007), Oregonator, Scholarpedia 2(5):1386, doi:10.4249/scholarpedia.1386, equations 4–6 and epsilon_prime scaling; https://www.scholarpedia.org/article/Oregonator . Model origin: Field RJ and Noyes RM (1974), J Chem Phys 60:1877-1884, doi:10.1063/1.1681288. Existing epsilon/q/initial values retained as explicit teaching parameters.
